## Overview

Geographic analysis helps find health disparities and target interventions. This guide maps two aimag-level indicators, maternal and infant mortality, and shows the steps that keep such maps honest: checking the counts, pooling small numbers, showing uncertainty, and comparing areas with a funnel plot rather than fixed colour bands.

## Getting Boundary Data

[mongolmaps](https://github.com/temuulene/mongolmaps) ships boundaries for every administrative level. Each unit carries its NSO code, so tables from mongolstats join by code rather than by name.

```{r boundaries, fig.alt="Map of Mongolia's 21 aimags and the capital, Ulaanbaatar, with each unit labelled"}
aimags <- mn_aimags() # 21 aimags and Ulaanbaatar
aimags |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(name, nso_code, iso_code, area_km2) |>
  head()

mn_map(aimags, label = TRUE, title = "Mongolia's 21 Aimags and Ulaanbaatar") +
  analysis_map_theme()
```

Other levels work the same way: `mn_regions()`, `mn_soums()`, `mn_ub_districts()` and `mn_khoroos()`. (mongolstats' own geoBoundaries helpers, `mn_boundaries()` and the name-based joins, are deprecated in favour of mongolmaps.)

### Region codes in NSO tables

NSO's `Region` dimension mixes levels: `"0"` is the national total, `"1"`–`"4"` are the four economic regions, `"5"` is Ulaanbaatar as a region, and three-digit codes are aimags. `mn_join()` keeps the aimag level and drops the rest. Many health tables store Ulaanbaatar's figures only under the region code `"5"` and leave its aimag-level code `"511"` empty; `mn_join()` notices this and takes the capital's values from the region row, with a message, so no recoding is needed.

## Case Study: Maternal Mortality

Maternal deaths are rare: Mongolia records a few dozen a year, and most aimags record none in a typical year. A single year's maternal mortality ratio (MMR) by aimag can be very unstable. We pool up to 10 common calendar years, retain incomplete counts as missing, and attach conditional Poisson intervals. A maternal death is a death during pregnancy or within 42 days of its end from a cause related to or aggravated by pregnancy or its management, excluding accidental or incidental causes. Confirm that the source applies this definition. MMR uses live births as its denominator; it is different from maternal mortality per woman-years.

### Check the counts before mapping

Aimag codes start with their region's digit (`1xx` = Western, `2xx` = Khangai, `3xx` = Central, `4xx` = Eastern), so aimag counts should add up to their regional subtotal. Reconciliation detects inconsistencies, but cannot identify which source entry is wrong.

```{r maternal-check}
# Report both inconsistent and uncheckable subtotals. Never infer zero.
subtotal_mismatches <- function(data) {
  analysis_keys(data, c("Region", "period"))
  aimag_sums <- data |>
    filter(nchar(Region) == 3, Region != "511") |>
    mutate(region = substr(Region, 1, 1)) |>
    summarise(aimag_sum = analysis_sum(value), .by = c(region, period))
  region_totals <- data |>
    filter(Region %in% as.character(1:4)) |>
    select(region = Region, period, region_total = value)
  full_join(aimag_sums, region_totals, by = join_by(region, period), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
    mutate(check = case_when(
      !is.finite(aimag_sum) | !is.finite(region_total) ~ "Uncheckable",
      aimag_sum != region_total ~ "Needs review",
      .default = "Agrees"
    )) |>
    filter(check != "Agrees")
}
annual_tbl <- "DT_NSO_2100_002V1"
monthly_tbl <- "DT_NSO_2100_002V2"
maternal_annual <- nso_data(annual_tbl, list(
  Region = nso_dim_values(annual_tbl, "Region")$code,
  Year = nso_dim_values(annual_tbl, "Year", labels = "en")$label_en
), labels = "en") |> mutate(period = Year_en)
maternal_monthly <- nso_data(monthly_tbl, list(
  Region = nso_dim_values(monthly_tbl, "Region")$code,
  Month = nso_table_periods(monthly_tbl)$label
), labels = "en") |> mutate(period = Month_en)
annual_checks <- subtotal_mismatches(maternal_annual)
monthly_checks <- subtotal_mismatches(maternal_monthly)
count(annual_checks, check)
count(monthly_checks, check)
filter(annual_checks, check == "Needs review")
```

An aimag sum larger than its regional total indicates a source inconsistency, not which entry is incorrect. Missing totals or component observations are labelled uncheckable. The monthly source is used provisionally below; national reconciliation cannot establish the meaning of every blank cell. Record unresolved discrepancies for follow-up with NSO before publication.

### Pooled maternal mortality ratio

The MMR divides maternal deaths by live births (`DT_NSO_2100_018V5`) over the same common calendar years. A pooled result is a birth-weighted summary of the selected period, not an estimate of current-year risk.

```{r maternal-data}
units <- c("0", setdiff(mn_aimags()$nso_code, "511"), "5")
maternal_source <- analysis_fetch_counts(monthly_tbl, units)
birth_source <- analysis_fetch_counts("DT_NSO_2100_018V5", units)
complete_years <- analysis_common_years(maternal_source$annual, birth_source$annual)
stopifnot(length(complete_years) > 0L)
mmr_years <- tail(complete_years, 10L)
mmr_period <- paste(range(mmr_years), collapse = "-")
maternal_deaths <- analysis_pool_counts(maternal_source$annual, mmr_years)
live_births <- analysis_pool_counts(birth_source$annual, mmr_years)
mmr <- analysis_pair(
  select(maternal_deaths, Region, Region_en, deaths = count, missing_deaths = n_missing),
  select(live_births, Region, births = count, missing_births = n_missing), "Region"
)
mmr <- bind_cols(mmr, analysis_poisson(mmr$deaths, mmr$births, 1e5)) |>
  rename(mmr = rate) |>
  mutate(Region_en = trimws(Region_en))
national_mmr <- filter(mmr, Region == "0")
stopifnot(nrow(national_mmr) == 1L, is.finite(national_mmr$mmr))
mmr_units <- filter(mmr, Region != "0")
stopifnot(nrow(mmr_units) == 22L)
mmr_units |>
  transmute(
    area = Region_en, deaths, births,
    missing_months = paste(missing_deaths, missing_births, sep = " / "),
    estimate = if_else(is.finite(mmr), sprintf("%.1f (%.1f–%.1f)", mmr, lower, upper), "Insufficient data")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Area", "Maternal deaths", "Live births", "Missing months: deaths / births", "MMR per 100,000 (95% CI)"),
    digits = 0, format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )

# Sensitivity: remove the pandemic years; use the same validation rules.
sensitivity_years <- setdiff(mmr_years, as.character(2020:2022))
stopifnot(length(sensitivity_years) > 0L)
sensitivity <- analysis_pair(
  select(analysis_pool_counts(maternal_source$annual, sensitivity_years), Region, deaths = count),
  select(analysis_pool_counts(birth_source$annual, sensitivity_years), Region, births = count), "Region"
) |> mutate(mmr = if_else(is.finite(deaths) & births > 0, deaths / births * 1e5, NA_real_))
filter(sensitivity, Region == "0") |>
  transmute(Period = paste(range(sensitivity_years), collapse = "–"), `National MMR per 100,000` = mmr) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "National estimate excluding pandemic years")
```

Unresolved source values are not converted to zero. `r if (run_vignette) sum(!is.finite(mmr_units$mmr)) else "Some"` areas have insufficient observations for the pooled estimate and appear grey on the map. Inspect `maternal_source$status` and `birth_source$status` before considering any table-specific recode. Conditional Poisson intervals do not include registration error, geographic mismatch or denominator uncertainty.

Over `r if (run_vignette) mmr_period else "the selected period"`, the national recorded MMR was `r if (run_vignette) round(national_mmr$mmr) else "-"` per 100,000 live births. The national estimate excluding 2020-2022 is shown above. Pooling can reduce random variation but cannot repair missing observations or systematic error.

### Choropleth and confidence intervals

```{r maternal-map, fig.height=if (run_vignette && any(is.finite(mmr_units$mmr))) 5 else 2.4, fig.alt=if (run_vignette && any(is.finite(mmr_units$mmr))) "Choropleth map of the pooled maternal mortality ratio by aimag and Ulaanbaatar over the selected complete years" else "No area has a complete observed estimate for a maternal mortality map"}
mmr_map <- mn_join(mmr_units, by = "Region", level = "aimag")
stopifnot(nrow(mmr_map) == 22L, !anyDuplicated(mmr_map$nso_code))

if (!any(is.finite(mmr_units$mmr))) {
  ggplot() +
    annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "No area has a complete observed estimate", size = 5, color = "#536873") +
    labs(
      title = "Maternal Mortality Map Is Not Available",
      subtitle = "Missing observations prevent an area comparison",
      caption = "Source: NSO Mongolia, DT_NSO_2100_002V2 and DT_NSO_2100_018V5"
    ) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#183442"))
} else {
  mn_map(mmr_map, fill = mmr, title = paste0("Maternal Mortality Ratio, ", mmr_period)) +
    labs(
      subtitle = "Per 100,000 live births; grey = insufficient data",
      fill = "MMR\n(per 100k)",
      caption = "Pooled recorded counts | Source: NSO Mongolia"
    ) +
    guides(fill = guide_colourbar(barwidth = grid::unit(85, "mm"), barheight = grid::unit(3, "mm"))) +
    analysis_map_theme()
}
```

A map shows point estimates only. The interval plot shows how uncertain each one is:

```{r maternal-intervals, fig.alt=if (run_vignette && any(is.finite(mmr_units$mmr))) "Dot plot of maternal mortality ratios with exact 95% confidence intervals and a dashed national reference" else "No area has a complete observed estimate or confidence interval for maternal mortality", fig.height=if (run_vignette && any(is.finite(mmr_units$mmr))) 7 else 2.4}
if (!any(is.finite(mmr_units$mmr))) {
  ggplot() +
    annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "No area has a complete observed estimate", size = 5, color = "#536873") +
    labs(
      title = "Maternal Mortality Intervals Are Not Available",
      subtitle = "Missing observations prevent area estimates and confidence intervals",
      caption = "Source: NSO Mongolia, DT_NSO_2100_002V2 and DT_NSO_2100_018V5"
    ) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#183442"))
} else {
  mmr_units |>
    filter(is.finite(mmr)) |>
    mutate(Region_en = forcats::fct_reorder(Region_en, mmr)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = mmr, y = Region_en)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = national_mmr$mmr, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.3, color = "grey60", orientation = "y") +
    geom_point(color = "#A94438", size = 2.5) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Maternal Mortality Ratio by Aimag, ", mmr_period),
      subtitle = "Per 100,000 live births, with exact 95% CIs; dashed line = national ratio",
      x = "Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births",
      y = NULL,
      caption = "Source: NSO Mongolia, DT_NSO_2100_002V2 and DT_NSO_2100_018V5"
    ) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
```

Intervals can remain wide after pooling. Zero observed maternal deaths has a positive upper Poisson limit and is not evidence of zero risk. Missing data is a different state and is not shown as zero. Compare the pandemic-excluded result before describing a pooled pattern as typical.

## Case Study: Infant Mortality

### Funnel plot

A **funnel plot** places each area's recorded IMR against its number of births. Conservative discrete Poisson limits are wider for smaller denominators. A point outside the limits is unusual under a common-rate Poisson model, not proof that the difference cannot be due to chance or that care is worse. Unmeasured heterogeneity, referral, data quality and overdispersion can affect the interpretation.

```{r imr-funnel-data}
infant_source <- analysis_fetch_counts("DT_NSO_2100_014V1", units)
imr_year <- analysis_latest(analysis_common_years(infant_source$annual, birth_source$annual))
infant_deaths <- filter(infant_source$annual, year == imr_year)
imr_births <- filter(birth_source$annual, year == imr_year)
imr <- analysis_pair(
  select(infant_deaths, Region, Region_en, deaths = count),
  select(imr_births, Region, births = count), "Region"
) |> mutate(Region_en = trimws(Region_en))
imr <- bind_cols(imr, analysis_poisson(imr$deaths, imr$births)) |> rename(imr = rate)
national_rate <- with(filter(imr, Region == "0"), deaths / births)
stopifnot(length(national_rate) == 1L, is.finite(national_rate), national_rate > 0)

# Discrete quantiles give conservative attainable tail probabilities.
# Step-shaped limits are expected; no interpolation is used for classification.
funnel_limit <- function(births, p) qpois(p, births * national_rate) / births * 1000
imr_units <- filter(imr, Region != "0") |>
  mutate(signal = analysis_funnel_signal(deaths, births, national_rate))
count(imr_units, signal)
```

```{r imr-funnel-plot, fig.alt="Funnel plot of infant mortality rate against number of live births by aimag, with 95% and 99.8% control limits around the national rate"}
funnel <- tibble::tibble(births = exp(seq(log(200), log(max(imr_units$births) * 1.1), length.out = 300))) |>
  mutate(
    lower_998 = funnel_limit(births, 0.001), upper_998 = funnel_limit(births, 0.999),
    lower_95 = funnel_limit(births, 0.025), upper_95 = funnel_limit(births, 0.975)
  )

signal_colors <- c("Above 95% limit" = "#C2623D", "Within limits" = "grey55", "Below 95% limit" = "#167D8D", "Insufficient data" = "grey85")

ggplot(filter(imr_units, is.finite(imr), births > 0), aes(x = births, y = imr)) +
  geom_line(data = funnel, aes(y = upper_998), linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
  geom_line(data = funnel, aes(y = lower_998), linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
  geom_line(data = funnel, aes(y = upper_95), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_line(data = funnel, aes(y = lower_95), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = national_rate * 1000, color = "grey20") +
  geom_point(aes(color = signal), size = 2.5) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(imr_units, is.finite(imr), signal != "Within limits" | Region == "5"),
    aes(label = Region_en), size = 3, color = "grey20", min.segment.length = 0, seed = 1
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = signal_colors, name = NULL) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Funnel Plot of Infant Mortality by Aimag, ", imr_year),
    subtitle = "Solid line = national rate; dashed = 95% limits; dotted = 99.8% limits",
    x = "Live births (log scale)",
    y = "Infant deaths per 1,000 live births",
    caption = "Source: NSO Mongolia, DT_NSO_2100_014V1 and DT_NSO_2100_018V5"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

### Mapping the signals

```{r imr-signal-map, fig.alt="Map of aimags classified as above, within, or below the 95% funnel limits for infant mortality"}
imr_map <- mn_join(imr_units, by = "Region", level = "aimag")
stopifnot(nrow(imr_map) == 22L, !anyDuplicated(imr_map$nso_code))

mn_map(imr_map, fill = signal, title = paste0("Infant Mortality Compared with the National Rate, ", imr_year)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = signal_colors, na.value = "grey90", name = NULL) +
  labs(subtitle = "Classified by 95% funnel limits around the national rate. Data: NSO Mongolia") +
  analysis_map_theme() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1))
```

With 22 units, roughly one flag at 95% would be expected under an ideal common-rate model; discrete limits can be conservative, and the estimated national reference includes each area. The 99.8% limits are a stricter screen, not a blanket multiple-comparison correction. A signal warrants investigation of source definitions, quality, referral and other differences. If births and deaths are assigned by occurrence rather than residence, referrals may distort area comparisons; that assignment rule must be confirmed for these tables.

## Tips for Spatial Epidemiology

1. **Check the counts first**: Make sure aimags add up to regional and national totals before you pool or map.
2. **Build rates from counts**: Sum numerators and denominators over the period, then divide. Do not average monthly or annual rates.
3. **Pool rare events**: Combine several years for rare outcomes such as maternal deaths.
4. **Show uncertainty**: Pair every choropleth with confidence intervals or a funnel plot.
5. **State the screening model**: Funnel plots reflect denominator size under a stated model; inspect heterogeneity and missing data before interpreting flags.
6. **Join by code**: `mongolmaps::mn_join()` matches NSO `Region` codes, so spelling differences cannot drop an aimag from the map.
